b:
Father at work abroad,
mother at work at home,
and in between,
an only child,
I was lonely

He was the gift
that came
to end the cruelty
called my loneliness

His
white veshti
and khadi shirt
stay in the waves of my memory
as a treasure that never leaves

The elephant rides
I took
on his back
were as comforting
as a mother's lap

Even when visitors scolded me
for my cheeky mouth,
he was another father
who hugged me with tenderness

The pet quarrels we had,
he for the morning news
and I
for the cartoons,
stay as pictures in my heart
and as tears in my eyes

The shirt buttons
I fastened for him
when he could no longer manage
were my last closeness
with him

Perhaps because
he who told the whole village
"that boy will cure my illness"
left
without telling me,

I did not cry
that day,
I do not cry
today

One day I will go
and cure his illness

Until then he will wait
in my village,
in his house,
for me,
he
note: Periyappa is a father's elder brother. A veshti is the white cloth worn wrapped around the waist; khadi is hand-spun cotton.
